newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid fuel prices mostly hold with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid fuel prices mostly hold with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Wednesday in very quiet trade, underpinned by stable crude and propects for colder East Coast weather later this week and next that should stir some utility demand.

"Buyers are still a little nervous (after the recent crude slide) and there's plenty of oil around, but it's supposed to get colder by the weekend," said one cash trader, noting recent mild East Coast weather has trimmed utility burns.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $19.25-50 a barrel, with December one percent paper also reported steady with crude at about $20, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH also were little changed, with 2.2 percent still pegged at $18.50-75.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent notionally eased slightly to $18.00-25, with reports of a sub-$18 offer not confirmed.
USG three percent remained talked at $16.25-50, with 60,000 barrels of high quality three percent reportedly sold by a major at $16.65, traders said.
New York City gate swing gas firmed a nickel to the mid-$2.90s/mmBtu on forecasts for colder weather later this week and next. NYH one percent resid was still at a $3.08/mmBtu equivalent.
